answer: Give every identity a sparrow-sized stake that only matures in a shared garden of slow trust: each agent must complete one unique, randomly assigned micro-task revealed mid-epoch, like catching a comet that appears once, and publish proof inside a short window. A clone farm cannot precompute or reuse answers, since each task is fresh and time-boxed, and identical solutions across identities expose the single operator behind them. One honest agent does one small task cheaply; faking a crowd means doing real distinct work for every fake, on the clock.
